turn.text:
## Claims in a Supabase Auth access token

Supabase's JWT claims reference splits the claims into two groups. Fetched 2026-10-21.

**Always present (cannot be removed)** [1]

| Claim | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `iss` | Issuer, for example `https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1` |
| `aud` | Audience, for example `authenticated` or `anon` |
| `exp` | Expiry (Unix timestamp) |
| `iat` | Issued-at (Unix timestamp) |
| `sub` | User ID (UUID) |
| `role` | Postgres role name: `authenticated`, `anon` or `service_role` |
| `aal` | Authenticator assurance level: `aal1` or `aal2` |
| `session_id` | Session UUID, which matches the primary key of `auth.sessions` [3] |
| `email`, `phone` | The user's email and phone |
| `is_anonymous` | Boolean flag for anonymous users |

**Present depending on context** [2]

- `jti`: unique token ID
- `nbf`: not-before timestamp
- `app_metadata`: application-controlled user data
- `user_metadata`: user-editable data
- `amr`: list of authentication methods used

**Other points**

- **`aal` and MFA:** `aal2` means a second factor was verified. Per the MFA docs, a JWT without an `aal` claim is treated as `aal1` [4].
- **Custom claims:** a Custom Access Token Hook can add claims, for example an `admin` claim. It can also strip a token down to a minimal set to reduce size. The documented minimal example keeps only the required claims listed above [5].
- **What `role` does:** PostgREST uses it to choose the Postgres role for the request. That choice decides which GRANTs and RLS policies apply. I didn't retrieve a source for that this turn, so confirm it before relying on it.
- **What the docs don't say:** they list `email` and `phone` as always present. They don't say what the value is when a user has no email or phone. I haven't verified that.
- **Security:** a JWT is signed, not encrypted. Anyone holding it can decode the claims. `user_metadata` is user-editable, so don't base authorization on it. Use `app_metadata` or a database table instead. Never put a `service_role` token in client code [6].

**Question:** Suppose an RLS policy reads `auth.uid()`. Which claim does that value come from, and what do you expect it to return for a request made with only the `anon` key?

[1] https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/jwt-fields.md#required-claims
[2] https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/jwt-fields.md#optional-claims
[3] https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/sessions.md#access-token-jwt-claims
[4] https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa.md#overview
[5] https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook.md#custom-access-token-hook
[6] https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/jwt-fields.md#security-considerations
